description: Canonical closed state machine for the single client-local durable transaction that carries one encrypted effective scope from the creator's explicit genesis intent to MLS write-ready. It is the machine-readable form of zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 5.1.2 and the only source a conforming client uses to decide what it must persist, in what order, and which single next arrow a recoverer may execute.
registry_rules: This record is client-local normative durable state protected by the device secret. It is not a wire object, not a Realm Event, not an Account Data key and not a server transaction. It MUST NOT enter the ak.realm.create payload, any current projection or query result, client sync or federation.

This registry constrains what a conforming client MUST persist and verify. It never authorizes a peer, a Station or a federation partner to believe another party's local state: every cross-party conclusion still comes from an exact accepted Event, and an assertion about this record carries no protocol weight.

The logical record key is exactly (owner_actor_id, effective_scope, operation) with operation fixed to mls_genesis. owner_actor_id MUST be the complete Account ActorId including its station_id for an ordinary human creator, and the complete ActorId of the Agent or service branch otherwise; a bare principal DID is not a key. effective_scope MUST be the canonical typed scope of zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 5.1, never a page route, a displayed Realm or a bare string alias.

The creator device and signer method are immutable fields of the record and are deliberately not part of the logical key, so a reload, a second window of the same account and a re-entry on the same device all find the same record, while a different device never silently opens a second Genesis. A device that does not hold this record's private state and signer MUST wait for the accepted result and proceed through Welcome, device migration or recovery; it MUST NOT take the record over and regenerate material.

Each local authoring vault holds at most one active record per (effective_scope, operation), enforced by a partial unique constraint or an equivalent atomic compare-and-swap. A process lock, a UI guard or a de-duplicated effect is not protocol mutual exclusion; mutual exclusion across devices remains the single accepted-Genesis slot of the same effective scope.

The closed creation intent MAY be amended in place, and only while the record is at genesis_intent_persisted. An amendment is one atomic durable replacement of the whole closed intent under the unchanged logical key, never a partial patch of a single selector, and it is registered as the self transition genesis_intent_persisted_to_genesis_intent_persisted. From realm_accepted on, and in every terminal state, the intent is immutable; a creator who wants a different selector must finish this attempt or reach a terminal state and open a new attempt generation.

This transaction applies to effective_scope.kind realm and circle only. effective_scope.kind="sidecar" keeps the independent handshake profile of zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.5.1 and is out of scope here; a client MUST NOT open this record for a sidecar scope.

A recoverer reads the durable record and executes the single next arrow its current state allows. A retryable transport failure, a page reload, a process crash and an unavailable accepted-Genesis query do not change the logical state. Rebuilding material from UI state is never a recovery path.
Any change to a field of an active attempt after the Genesis is signed is not a retry and MUST fail closed. A second window or a background effect may only join the existing record.

The selector is read only from the formal transaction record. A local draft without that record follows the retention rules: converge on an existing accepted Genesis, discard the draft when there is definitely none, and stay unwritable while the accepted state is unknown.

The ak.mls.genesis genesis_timestamp_contract in canonical contract-registry.json applies to every Genesis, including Sidecar outside this FSM. Freeze one canonical authoring timestamp for both outer Event.created_at and payload.created_at in the unsigned core. Signing, queueing and recovery preserve the exact bytes. Independently revalidate equality before accepting own completion or a competing accepted winner; invalid accepted evidence leaves the client unwritable and MUST NOT trigger superseded or material regeneration. Producer-proof and Station commit timestamps remain independent.
Adding a state, an arrow or a required durable field requires an active vector-registry.json row that injects a crash and a reload on both sides of the new arrow in the same registry release.

record_identity.active_record_uniqueness: one active record per (effective_scope, operation) per local authoring vault, enforced by a partial unique constraint or an equivalent atomic compare-and-swap
record_identity.protocol_mutual_exclusion: the single accepted ak.mls.genesis slot of the same effective scope

scope_kind_applicability.rule: effective_scope.kind="sidecar" keeps the independent handshake profile of zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.5.1; this transaction does not change the Sidecar contract. A conforming client MUST NOT open, resume or key this record on a sidecar scope, and a Sidecar handshake MUST NOT be read as an instance of this state machine.

proposal_carrier_contract.identity_and_scope_rule: sender_actor_id is the complete owner_actor_id and target_scope equals proposed_group_genesis_binding.effective_scope field by field.
proposal_carrier_contract.genesis_rule: base_group_state_ref is null and previous_epoch, next_epoch and key_access_revision are all the unsigned integer 0.

required_durable_fields: the exact accepted scope-create Event and covering Commit
the independently verified nonce-bound current authority bundle and complete authority chain
the verified complete authorized current cut proving no accepted Genesis for the exact effective scope
the exact current creator Actor, device and signer authorization evidence
the canonical closed local proposal carrier bytes and their digest
the single governance_binding copied unchanged from the durable proposal
governance_evidence_contract.genesis_absence_rule: Only a cryptographically verified complete authorized current cut covering the exact effective scope proves absence. Missing rows in an incomplete projection, HTTP not_found alone, a timeout or an unavailable read do not prove absence. An accepted Genesis winner moves to superseded rather than regenerating material.
governance_evidence_contract.creator_authority_rule: The complete owner ActorId, creator device and signer method must match the immutable intent and the accepted creator and current endpoint authorization at this cut. A principal-only match or another Station/device cannot take over the record.
governance_evidence_contract.binding_rule: The canonical local proposal carrier uses the same durable proposed_group_genesis_binding unchanged: exact effective scope and derived group id, null base_group_state_ref, and unsigned previous_epoch, next_epoch and key_access_revision equal to zero.
governance_evidence_contract.wire_rule: No proof RPC, proof request/outcome carrier, new operation or new wire field is introduced. Existing authority/current evidence remains independently verified; the local proposal is not a Station-signed governance outcome.
governance_evidence_contract.unavailable_rule: Unknown, unauthenticated, incomplete or inconsistent evidence leaves realm_accepted unchanged and prohibits random generation, blob upload, signing and enqueue.

immutable_fields: the associated exact signed Realm-create unit and the create Event id derived from it
selector_amendment.rationale: The proposed group genesis binding is forbidden in the ak.realm.create payload by construction, so replacing it invalidates neither an already signed nor an in-flight create unit; every consumer of the selector, the selector-dependent random material and the pinned governance binding first runs after realm_accepted. While the record is still at genesis_intent_persisted the creator has therefore chosen nothing that anyone else can already have observed.
selector_amendment.exit_rule: Amendment is legal only inside genesis_intent_persisted. From realm_accepted on, and in every terminal state, the closed intent is immutable: the only ways forward are to finish this attempt or to reach a terminal state and open a new attempt generation, which inherits the selector from the original durable intent.

forbidden_carriers: any current result or query projection
disclosure_boundary.peer_trust_rule: A conforming implementation MUST NOT accept another party's assertion about this record as evidence of scope state. Genesis existence, the creator coordinates, the locked selectors and write-readiness are decided only from exact accepted Events.

states.entry_predicate: The record is committed atomically before the first network side effect of ak.realm.create, before any governance-evidence read, and before any selector-dependent random material is generated. An already accepted MLS Realm that has no accepted Genesis enters here with this state's postconditions already satisfied and immediately continues to realm_accepted; no entry path may generate random material or read governance evidence before the selector is durable.
required_durable_fields: logical key: owner_actor_id, effective_scope, operation
complete owner_actor_id including its station_id
creator signer slot bound to this authoring device
canonical effective scope and the mls_group_id derived from it
the complete closed proposed_group_genesis_binding
the associated exact signed Realm-create unit and the create Event id derived from it
states.retry_rule: A retry re-reads this record and continues from it. It MUST NOT re-read the proposed binding from UI state, a default, a Realm profile, an accepted history facet or any projection. A creator who changes the selection while the record is still in this state does not open a second attempt: the whole closed intent is replaced atomically through genesis_intent_persisted_to_genesis_intent_persisted.

states.entry_predicate: The client obtained an accepted ak.realm.create from its own Station, either as the submit result or by exact resolve, and an exact accepted-Genesis query for this scope returned a definite absent. An unknown result, a timeout or a missing projection MUST NOT enter this state.
required_durable_fields: accepted Realm-create Event id and the digest of its exact accepted bytes
the Realm digest suite
the accepted authority-root resolution result
every field of the previous state, which stays immutable
states.retry_rule: Repeat the exact accepted-Genesis query. A definite absent keeps the state, a definite winner moves to superseded, and anything else leaves the state unchanged.

states.entry_predicate: The client independently verifies the current authority chain and nonce-bound bundle, the exact accepted scope-create Event and Commit, the complete authorized current cut proving Genesis absence for this exact scope, and the current creator Actor/device/signer authority. The canonical local proposal retains the exact durable intent scope, derived group id, null base and three zero values. These inputs are pinned together before any dependent randomness; a local proposal alone is never Station evidence.
required_durable_fields: the exact accepted scope-create Event and covering Commit
the independently verified nonce-bound current authority bundle and complete authority chain
the verified complete authorized current cut proving no accepted Genesis for the exact effective scope
the exact current creator Actor, device and signer authorization evidence
the canonical closed local proposal carrier bytes and their digest
the single governance_binding copied unchanged from the durable proposal
states.retry_rule: Before the pin commit, repeat existing authority and authorized current reads using the same durable selector and fresh transport nonce. Unknown authority, incomplete coverage or an unavailable Genesis decision keeps realm_accepted and generates no MLS material. Once pinned, reuse the exact evidence and local binding; do not replace them with a refreshed cut or UI projection.

states.entry_predicate: The MLS engine produced epoch 0 using only the binding pinned by the previous state, and the whole recovery unit below was durably committed before any public blob upload, any signature and any enqueue.
required_durable_fields: device-secret-encrypted epoch-0 private group state
cipher suite
creator leaf and signer binding
the raw GroupInfo and ratchet tree bytes together with their content-addressed refs
the frozen created_at
the exact unsigned Genesis core
states.retry_rule: A crash before this commit that produced no externally observable material is not a recoverable attempt, and the recoverer regenerates epoch 0 from the same pinned binding. Once any of this material can be observed outside the device, this durable unit MUST already exist and MUST NOT be regenerated.

states.entry_predicate: The public blobs were written to a durable object store resolvable by the service that hosts this Realm and verified against their refs, the exact Genesis was signed, and the transaction update plus the durable outbound enqueue succeeded inside one local atomic commit.
required_durable_fields: the immutable Genesis Event id
the exact signed Event bytes
the canonical bytes digest of those bytes
the outbound_queue_item_id of the associated ledger item
the public blob refs
states.retry_rule: The worker may only resend the frozen bytes. After a lost response the client first queries the exact accepted Genesis: a match advances to genesis_accepted, a definite absent with a retryable last result keeps the same queue item, and an unknown result keeps the state. An exhausted queue, an HTTP 2xx, a duplicate code and a completed UI effect never advance the transaction. Re-signing, rebuilding MLS state and replacing the proof basis are forbidden from this state on.

states.entry_predicate: An exact accepted-Event resolve from the client's own Station returned a Genesis whose bytes are byte-identical to the bytes frozen at enqueue. HTTP success, a duplicate code and a locally derived Event id are all insufficient.
required_durable_fields: the accepted Event id
the exact accepted bytes and their digest
the accepted-at and result binding
the queue item, kept as completed-but-retained until local artifacts converge
states.retry_rule: Re-resolving the same accepted Event is idempotent. A resolve that returns different accepted Genesis bytes for this scope is an unexplainable inconsistency, not a retry.

states.entry_predicate: The accepted artifact consumer installed the accepted Genesis Event, the matching epoch-0 private state and the raw GroupInfo and ratchet-tree bytes and refs as one winning epoch, and committed that install durably.
required_durable_fields: the accepted artifact record or ref
the private-state binding
the public-material binding
the complete consistency check results
states.retry_rule: A partially persisted install is retried as a whole. Any single mismatch moves the record to quarantined; a partially ready scope does not exist.

states.entry_predicate: The client re-read durable state instead of trusting an in-memory flag, confirmed genesis_accepted, artifacts_converged and an exact private-state match, and published this state together with the MLS write-ready index in one durable commit.
required_durable_fields: minimal terminal receipt: the logical key, the accepted Genesis Event id and digest, the immutable Genesis binding, the accepted artifact ref and the ready commit position
states.retry_rule: A crash around this commit leaves either artifacts_converged with the last step retryable, or ready and the send-gate index both visible. A ready flag visible without the artifact record is an inconsistency, not a retry state.

states.entry_predicate: The exact signed Genesis received a definite terminal rejection, and queue retry stopped.
required_durable_fields: the Event id and digest of the rejected bytes
the original reason code
the stage at which the rejection occurred
the last verified accepted-or-absent result
states.retry_rule: A new attempt generation may open only after an exact query again confirms that no accepted Genesis exists, and only by atomically closing the previous attempt inside the same logical record. The selector is inherited from the original durable intent and MUST NOT be re-read from UI state, a default or a facet.

states.entry_predicate: An exact query found that a different Genesis is already accepted for this effective scope.
required_durable_fields: the winning Genesis Event id and its immutable binding
the loser Event id and digest, when this record had signed one
states.retry_rule: None. The local loser queue item is stopped and removed, the local private state MUST NOT be matched to the winner and MUST NOT become ready, and the scope proceeds only through Welcome, device migration or recovery.

states.entry_predicate: The local record, the queue item, the private state, the public refs, the signed bytes or the accepted result disagree in a way that has no single explanation.
required_durable_fields: the logical key
the last state
the invariant that failed
the Event id and digest
the outbound_queue_item_id
the accepted winner, when one is known
the reason code and the time of detection
states.retry_rule: None. Automatic authoring, queue retry and the send gate all stop. Clearing a flag and starting over is not a repair.

transitions.commit_boundary: The selector record is committed atomically before the first network side effect of ak.realm.create, before any governance-evidence read and before any selector-dependent random material.
transitions.crash_before_commit: No attempt exists. The next run starts from an explicit selection and MUST NOT infer a selector from a Realm that may already have been created.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The record exists and the recoverer continues from genesis_intent_persisted, reusing the frozen selector and the derived create Event id.

transitions.commit_boundary: The complete closed creation intent, including the regenerated proposed_group_genesis_binding, is replaced in one atomic durable commit under the unchanged logical key. A partial patch of the binding alone is not a legal write, and the commit MUST still precede the first governance-evidence read and any selector-dependent random material.
transitions.crash_before_commit: The previous closed intent is still the only durable one, and the recoverer continues from it. A selector shown in the UI but never committed authorizes nothing.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The replacement is the only durable intent, the superseded selector is unreadable, and the frozen Realm-create unit, its derived create Event id and the immutable record fields are unchanged.

transitions.commit_boundary: The accepted Realm-create result and the definite Genesis-absent result are committed together into the same record.
transitions.crash_before_commit: The recoverer resolves the create Event id already derived from the frozen unit. It MUST NOT submit a second create and MUST NOT read an unknown result as absent.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The record is at realm_accepted and the recoverer verifies existing authority and authorized current evidence using the frozen selector.

transitions.commit_boundary: The complete independently verified accepted authority/current/creator evidence and canonical local proposal are pinned together in one commit.
transitions.crash_before_commit: Existing authority and authorized current reads are repeated with the same durable selector and fresh transport nonce. A lost response never authorizes generating MLS or HPKE material.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The pinned verified evidence and unchanged local binding are reused and MUST NOT be replaced by a refreshed cut or an unverified projection.

transitions.commit_boundary: The epoch-0 private state, the public raw bytes, every randomness-dependent archive and the exact unsigned Genesis core are committed as one recovery unit.
transitions.crash_before_commit: Nothing was externally observable, so the recoverer regenerates epoch 0 from the same pinned binding.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The recoverer reuses the persisted epoch-0 material and MUST NOT regenerate randomness.

transitions.commit_boundary: The exact signed Event bytes and the outbound queue item are established in one atomic commit.
transitions.crash_before_commit: A signature produced but never committed together with a queue item is discarded, and the recoverer signs the same exact unsigned core again. Public blobs already uploaded are content-addressed, so they are re-verified rather than re-minted.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The frozen bytes are the only retriable original. There is no legal state in which the transaction committed without the queue item, and none in which the queue item is sendable while the transaction does not know its bytes.

transitions.commit_boundary: The exact accepted bytes and the accepted Event id are committed after an exact accepted-Event resolve.
transitions.crash_before_commit: A lost send response leaves the state unchanged, and the recoverer queries the exact accepted Genesis before resending the frozen bytes.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The record is at genesis_accepted and the queue item stays completed-but-retained until local artifacts converge.

transitions.commit_boundary: The accepted Event, the matching epoch-0 private state and the public material are installed as one winning epoch in one durable commit.
transitions.crash_before_commit: A partially persisted install is retried as a whole, and no partial install may report convergence.
transitions.crash_after_commit: The record is at artifacts_converged and only the ready publication remains.

transitions.commit_boundary: The ready state and the MLS send-gate index are published in one durable commit.
transitions.crash_before_commit: The record stays at artifacts_converged, the last step is retried and the send gate stays closed.
transitions.crash_after_commit: Both the ready state and the send-gate index are visible. A ready flag without the artifact record, and an open send gate without the ready state, are both inconsistencies.

atomic_cut_points.rule: genesis_intent_persisted MUST precede the first network side effect of ak.realm.create. The create Event id is derivable from the exact signed unit before submission, so the absence of an accepted realm id never justifies deferring the selector.

governance_result_pinned MUST precede any MLS or HPKE random material that depends on that binding. Evidence reads are retryable before the pin commit, but adopted verified evidence and the local binding MUST NOT be silently replaced by an unverified projection or an updated cut.

The epoch-0 private state, the public raw bytes, the randomness-dependent archive or ciphertext and the exact unsigned Genesis core MUST be committed as one recovery unit before public blobs are uploaded, before the Genesis is signed and before it is enqueued. A crash during purely in-memory generation that produced no external side effect is not a recoverable attempt; once any of that material can be observed externally, this durable unit MUST already exist.

The exact signed Event bytes and the outbound queue item MUST be established atomically. There is no legal state in which the transaction committed without the queue item, and none in which the queue item is sendable while the transaction does not yet know its bytes.

The ready state and the effective send-gate index MUST be published atomically. After a crash the client is either still at artifacts_converged with the last step retryable, or both are visible; a ready flag forked from the artifact record is forbidden.

transaction_owns: which single signed Genesis is the only retriable original
outbound_queue_binding.association_rule: Entering genesis_queued binds the two one-to-one inside a single durable commit through the Event id, the canonical bytes digest and the outbound_queue_item_id.
outbound_queue_binding.worker_rule: The generic outbound worker may only resend the frozen bytes. After a response loss the client first queries the exact accepted Genesis: a match advances to genesis_accepted, a definite absent with a retryable last result continues the same queue item, and an unknown result keeps the current state.
non_completion_signals: a local emitted or submitted flag

retention.before_ready: The selector, the pinned verified evidence and local proposal, the epoch-0 private state, the signed Event bytes and the queue association MUST NOT be deleted.
retention.at_ready: One atomic compaction MAY delete the pre-Genesis proposal, the pinned verification evidence copies, staged state and the completed queue item. The accepted private group state, the accepted artifact, the public blobs the protocol still requires to be resolvable, and the minimal terminal receipt MUST be retained; protocol retention of the public blobs MUST NOT be garbage-collected together with local temporary files.
retention.terminal_attempt: Mismatched secrets of a rejected or superseded attempt, and temporary blobs that no accepted Event references, may be erased only after the terminal diagnostics are durable, the queue is stopped and the accepted state has been confirmed again.
retention.quarantined: Original recovery material is not erased automatically.
retention.tombstone_rule: Physical deletion MUST NOT remove the tombstone recording that this logical key already had a terminal attempt.
